records.prompt: The supplied graph is the graph of \(f'(x)\) for a function \(f\) whose domain is \(-3<x<5\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For what values of \(x\) does \(f\) have a relative maximum? Justify.
parts.answer: The derivative changes from positive to negative at \(x=-2\). Therefore \(\boxed{x=-2}\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For what values of \(x\) does \(f\) have a relative minimum? Justify.
parts.answer: The derivative changes from negative to positive at \(x=4\). Therefore \(\boxed{x=4}\).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: On what intervals is the graph of \(f\) concave upward? Use \(f'\) to justify.
parts.answer: The graph of \(f\) is concave upward where \(f'\) is increasing: \(\boxed{(-1,1)\cup(3,5)}\).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Suppose \(f(1)=0\). Describe a sketch showing the general shape of \(f\) on \(0<x<2\).
parts.answer: On \((0,2)\), \(f'(x)<0\) except \(f'(1)=0\), so \(f\) is decreasing throughout. It is concave up on \((0,1)\), has a horizontal tangent at \((1,0)\) without an extremum, and is concave down on \((1,2)\).

records.prompt: Let \(R\) be the region in the first quadrant under \(y=1/\sqrt{x}\) for \(4\le x\le9\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If \(x=k\) divides \(R\) into two regions of equal area, find \(k\).
parts.answer: Half the area is \(1\), so \(2(\sqrt{k}-2)=1\). Hence \(\boxed{k=25/4}\).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid whose base is \(R\) and whose cross sections perpendicular to the \(x\)-axis are squares.
parts.answer: The square side is \(1/\sqrt{x}\), so \[V=\int_4^9\frac1x\,dx=\boxed{\ln(9/4)}.\]

records.prompt: The rate of cola consumption is \(S(t)=Ce^{kt}\), in billions of gallons per year, where \(t\) is years after the beginning of 1980.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: The rate doubles every 5 years and \(S(0)=6\). Find \(C\) and \(k\).
parts.answer: \(C=6\) and \(e^{5k}=2\), so \[\boxed{C=6,\qquad k=\frac{\ln2}{5}}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of consumption over the 10-year period beginning January 1, 1983.
parts.answer: \[\frac1{10}\int_3^{13}6e^{(\ln2)t/5}\,dt=\frac3{\ln2}\left(2^{13/5}-2^{3/5}\right)\approx\boxed{19.680}\] billion gallons per year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the trapezoidal rule with four equal subdivisions to estimate \(\int_5^7S(t)\,dt\).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Explain the meaning of \(\int_5^7S(t)\,dt\).
parts.answer: It is the total cola consumed in the United States from the beginning of 1985 to the beginning of 1987, measured in billions of gallons.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Sketch \(y=x+\sin x\) and \(y=x+3\sin x\).
parts.answer: Both graphs oscillate about the line \(y=x\). The first is nondecreasing with horizontal tangencies at odd multiples of \(\pi\); the second has alternating local extrema because \(1+3\cos x\) changes sign.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find all points where \(y=x+b\) is tangent to the graph of \(f\).
parts.answer: Intersection requires \(\sin x=1\), and then \(f'(x)=1+b\cos x=1\). On the interval, \[\boxed{x=-\frac{3\pi}{2},\ \frac\pi2}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Are these tangency points relative maxima of \(f\)? Justify.
parts.answer: Yes. At each point \(\sin x=1\), \(f''(x)=-b\sin x=-b<0\), so both are relative maxima.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Show that every inflection point lies on \(y=x\).
parts.answer: \(f''(x)=-b\sin x\). Concavity can change only at \(x=n\pi\). At each such point, \(f(n\pi)=n\pi\), so every inflection point has coordinates \((n\pi,n\pi)\) and lies on \(y=x\).

records.prompt: An oil tank is formed by revolving \(y=\frac{9}{625}x^4\), \(0\le x\le5\), about the \(y\)-axis. Oil enters at \(8\) cubic feet per minute.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the volume of the tank.
parts.answer: At height \(y\), \(x^2=\frac{25}{3}\sqrt{y}\). Thus \[V=\pi\int_0^9\frac{25}{3}\sqrt{y}\,dy=\boxed{150\pi\ \text{ft}^3}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: To the nearest minute, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
parts.answer: \[T=\frac{150\pi}{8}=18.75\pi\approx58.905,\] so \(\boxed{59\text{ minutes}}\).

parts.label: (e)
parts.prompt: Let \(h\) be the oil depth. Find \(dh/dt\) when \(h=4\).
parts.answer: \[V(h)=\frac{50\pi}{9}h^{3/2},\qquad 8=\frac{25\pi}{3}\sqrt{h}\frac{dh}{dt}.\] At \(h=4\), \[\boxed{\frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{12}{25\pi}\ \text{ft/min}}.\]

records.prompt: The line \(\ell\) passes through \((0,20)\) and is tangent at \(Q\) to \(y=x-\frac{x^2}{500}\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the \(x\)-coordinate of \(Q\).
parts.answer: If \(Q=(q,q-q^2/500)\), the tangent has slope \(1-q/250\) and \(y\)-intercept \(q^2/500\). Setting this equal to \(20\) gives \(q=100\). Thus \(\boxed{x_Q=100}\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Write an equation for \(\ell\).
parts.answer: The slope is \(1-100/250=3/5\), so \[\boxed{y=\frac35x+20}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A 50-foot vertical tree grows at the top of the hill. Does the spotlight along \(\ell\) strike the tree?
parts.answer: The hill has its top at \((250,125)\), so the tree occupies heights \(125\le y\le175\) at \(x=250\). The line gives \(y=\frac35(250)+20=170\). Hence \(\boxed{\text{yes}}\), it strikes the tree 45 feet above its base.
